requirements.title: READ is the data-transfer input statement and WRITE/PRINT are data-transfer output statements
requirements.definition: READ is the data transfer input statement; WRITE and PRINT are the data transfer output statements.

pending.read-data-transfer-input-statement: Use a future READ from a controlled internal or external record into an integer initialized to a distinct sentinel and assert the changed value after successful IOSTAT zero.
pending.write-data-transfer-output-statement: Use a future WRITE to an internal file prefilled with sentinel characters and assert exact produced characters; no external encoding or buffering is asserted.
pending.print-data-transfer-output-statement: Use PRINT only under a harness that captures the processor output unit portably; otherwise keep source classification pending and avoid comparing processor-dependent terminal formatting.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by opening a known file, writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a distinct labelled control path) and then observe only portable properties: successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, exact internal records or file existence where the source fixes it, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, storage encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific numeric status values are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself is a numbered syntax rule or numbered constraint, or otherwise requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle; unnumbered program restrictions are not promoted to required diagnostics.

requirements.title: A READ statement has parenthesized io-control-spec form or READ format form
requirements.definition: A read-stmt is READ with a parenthesized io-control-spec-list and optional input-item-list, or READ followed by a format and optional comma input-item-list.

pending.read-parenthesized-control-form: Positive-control source reads from an internal character record with READ(record,*) integer_sentinel and checks the changed value; malformed parentheses are repaired without changing the record.
pending.read-format-form: Positive-control source uses READ fmt_label, x with a labelled FORMAT and a controlled default input source once the owning input-unit rules are registered; the read changes x from a sentinel.
pending.read-optional-input-item-list: Use one READ with an input item initialized to a sentinel and one positioning/status READ with no input list only where later rules permit it; absence/presence of the list is the only syntax difference.

requirements.title: A WRITE statement has parenthesized io-control-spec form and optional output items
requirements.definition: A write-stmt is WRITE with a parenthesized io-control-spec-list and optional output-item-list.

pending.write-parenthesized-control-form: Positive-control source writes a distinct integer to an internal character variable initialized with sentinel characters and compares the resulting record to an independently derived string.
pending.write-optional-output-item-list: Positive-control source uses WRITE(buffer,"()") with no output-item-list for syntax admission and a separate WRITE(buffer,"(A)") "Q" with an output item; the item case preinitializes buffer with sentinel characters and checks "Q", while the no-item case is credited only for the admitted statement form.

requirements.title: A PRINT statement is PRINT format with optional output items
requirements.definition: A print-stmt is PRINT followed by a format and an optional comma output-item-list.

pending.print-format-required: Positive-control source compiles PRINT fmt_label, value with a labelled FORMAT in a complete program; a missing-format negative repairs only by adding the format, so syntax admission does not depend on terminal-output capture.
pending.print-optional-output-item-list: Positive-control sources compile both PRINT fmt_label and PRINT fmt_label, value in complete programs with the same labelled FORMAT where valid; the facet is a syntax-form plan and does not compare processor-dependent terminal output.

Examples of READ, WRITE, PRINT, and FORMAT; not normative.
Explanatory note about READ(name) and C1221; the owning constraint is outside this packet.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.5.7-12.6.1, the CLOSE statement and data transfer statements in general (batch152). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds. Round 1 found a conditional KEEP-on-nonexistent-file plan and scratch DELETE plans that observed only unit closure; both are now explicit no-portable-oracle reasons (no portable way to connect a nonexistent file with KEEP allowed; no portable name for a scratch file), while named-file DELETE keeps a portable EXIST= plan established before the CLOSE. Round 2 found the nonexistent-unit CLOSE plan relied on OPENED=.false.; it is now guarded on INQUIRE EXIST=.false., since no unit number is guaranteed nonexistent. The eight numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
